title: Associated primes after a flat base change (Bourbaki)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $M$ an $R$-module and $N$ an $S$-module which is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For a ring $T$ and a $T$-module $P$ call a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$ an associated prime of $P$ if $\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)=\{a\in T:az=0\}$ for some $z\in P$, and write $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ for the set of them. Then $$\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)\supseteq\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)}\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN),$$ where $M\otimes_RN$ is an $S$-module through $N$; and if $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], equality holds.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), lines 15774-15851 (statement 15774-15783, proof 15785-15851); tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags: 0312,algebra-lemma-bourbaki

proof.text: Throughout, $\varphi:R\to S$ is the ring map, $M\otimes_RN$ is an $S$-module through $N$, and every map $1_?\otimes(\cdot)$ or $(\cdot)\otimes1_N$ below is $S$-linear because $S$ acts on the factor $N$ only. Two remarks used repeatedly: an isomorphism of $T$-modules preserves annihilators of corresponding elements, hence associated primes; and every element of $S$ commutes with the $R$-action. *Inclusion $\supseteq$.* Let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$, say $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak p$ with $z\in M$. The $R$-linear map $R/\mathfrak p\to M$, $\bar r\mapsto rz$, is well defined and injective (its kernel is $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)/\mathfrak p=0$). Since $N$ is a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], $(R/\mathfrak p)\otimes_RN\to M\otimes_RN$ is injective, and it is $S$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1) the map $(R/\mathfrak p)\otimes_RN\to N/\mathfrak pN$, $\bar r\otimes n\mapsto rn\bmod\mathfrak pN$, is an isomorphism; it is $S$-linear since $s(rn)=r(sn)$. So $N/\mathfrak pN$ is isomorphic to an $S$-submodule of $M\otimes_RN$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-exact-sequence] (first inclusion, over the ring $S$) $\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)$. Taking the union over $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ gives the inclusion $\supseteq$ of the statement, for every ring $R$.

*Associated primes of a directed union.* Let $T$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a $T$-module and $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a family of submodules, directed (any two lie in a third) with $\bigcup_\lambda P_\lambda=P$. Then $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)=\bigcup_\lambda\operatorname{Ass}_T(P_\lambda)$: the inclusion $\supseteq$ is [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-exact-sequence] (first inclusion) for each inclusion $P_\lambda\subseteq P$; conversely if $\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)$ with $z\in P$, then $z\in P_\lambda$ for some $\lambda$, and the annihilator of $z$ as an element of $P_\lambda$ is the same ideal $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Lemma 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), proof, second paragraph: 'By definition of associated primes we see that ...'

proof.text: *Reduction to $M$ finite.* Assume $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; by Step 1 it remains to prove $\subseteq$. Let $(M_\lambda)$ be the family of finitely generated $R$-submodules of $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; it is directed ($M_\lambda+M_\mu$ is finitely generated) and its union is $M$ ($m\in Rm$). As $N$ is flat, each $M_\lambda\otimes_RN\to M\otimes_RN$ is injective [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] and $S$-linear; call its image $F_\lambda$. The $F_\lambda$ are directed ($M_\lambda\subseteq M_\mu$ gives $F_\lambda\subseteq F_\mu$, the maps being compatible) and their union is $M\otimes_RN$ (an element $\sum_{j=1}^km_j\otimes n_j$ lies in $F_\lambda$ as soon as $m_1,\dots,m_k\in M_\lambda$). By Step 2, over $S$ and over $R$: $\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)=\bigcup_\lambda\operatorname{Ass}_S(M_\lambda\otimes_RN)$ and $\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)=\bigcup_\lambda\operatorname{Ass}_R(M_\lambda)$. Hence if the inclusion $\subseteq$ holds for every $M_\lambda$, then $\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)\subseteq\bigcup_\lambda\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M_\lambda)}\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN)=\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)}\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN)$. So we may and do assume, in Steps 4-9, that $R$ is Noetherian and $M$ is a finite $R$-module.

*Claim C: if $R$ is Noetherian, $M$ a finite $R$-module and $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)$, then $\mathfrak p:=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$.* Steps 4-7 prove it. Put $P=M\otimes_RN$; $\mathfrak p$ is a prime ideal of $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-localize-at-prime] (over the ring $S$, at $\mathfrak q$) there is $w\in P_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_{S_{\mathfrak q}}(w)=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; $w\ne0$ since $\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}\ne S_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Lemma 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), proof, third paragraph: 'First we observe that qS_q ∈ Ass_{S_q}((M ⊗_R N)_q), see Lemma 0310. Let p be the corresponding prime of R.'

proof.text: *The identification $(M\otimes_RN)_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$.* Put $U=R\setminus\mathfrak p$. Since $\varphi(U)\subseteq S\setminus\mathfrak q$, every $u\in U$ acts invertibly on every $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module, so $N_{\mathfrak q}$, $P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $M\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$ (an $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module through $N_{\mathfrak q}$) are $R_{\mathfrak p}$-modules. (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] for $R\to A=S$, $T=S\setminus\mathfrak q$, the $S$-module $N$ and the $R$-module $M$ (and $M\otimes_RN\cong N\otimes_RM$), $P_{\mathfrak q}\cong M\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$ as $S_{\mathfrak q}$-modules, $(m\otimes n)/t\mapsto m\otimes(n/t)$. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] for $R\to A=R$ (identity), $T=U$, the $R$-module $M$ and the $R$-module $N_{\mathfrak q}$: $U^{-1}(M\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q})\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. (c) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-over-localization], applied to the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $M\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$, $U^{-1}(M\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q})\cong M\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$. All three isomorphisms are $R$-linear, so together $P_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$ compatibly with multiplication by each $a\in R$, which on $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is multiplication by $\varphi(a)/1\in S_{\mathfrak q}$ and on $M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$ is $(a\cdot)\otimes1$. (The source writes $M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}N_{\mathfrak q}$; tensoring over $R$ is the same module here and is what Step 7 needs.)

source.place: Lemma 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), proof, third paragraph: 'Note that (M ⊗_R N)_q = M ⊗_R N_q = M_p ⊗_{R_p} N_q'

proof.text: *$N_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat $R$-module.* Let $f:Q'\to Q$ be an injective $R$-linear map. Then $1_N\otimes f:N\otimes_RQ'\to N\otimes_RQ$ is injective because $N$ is $R$-flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and it is $S$-linear; localizing at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ keeps it injective [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] (applied to the exact sequence $0\to N\otimes_RQ'\to N\otimes_RQ$). By the naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (for $A=S$, $T=S\setminus\mathfrak q$, the $S$-module $N$) this localized map is $1_{N_{\mathfrak q}}\otimes f:N_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_RQ'\to N_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_RQ$, which is therefore injective. So $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat. (The source uses that $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$; flatness over $R$ is what the form of Step 5 needs.)

source.place: Lemma 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), proof, third paragraph: 'Since N_q is flat over R_p'

proof.text: *$\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$.* The ring $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finite $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module (if $m_1,\dots,m_k$ generate $M$ then $m/u=\sum(a_j/u)(m_j/1)$ for $m=\sum a_jm_j$) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}\notin\operatorname{Ass}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] there is $x\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ which is a nonzerodivisor on $M_{\mathfrak p}$; write $x=a/u$ with $a\in\mathfrak p$, $u\in U$. As $u$ acts bijectively on $M_{\mathfrak p}$, multiplication by $a$ on $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective. Since $N_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-flat (Step 6) [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $(a\cdot)\otimes1$ on $M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_RN_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective, so by Step 5 multiplication by $\varphi(a)/1$ on $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective. But $a\in\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ gives $\varphi(a)/1\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{Ann}_{S_{\mathfrak q}}(w)$, so $(\varphi(a)/1)w=0$ with $w\ne0$ (Step 4): a contradiction. Hence $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}\in\operatorname{Ass}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p})$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-prime-from-localization] $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$. This proves Claim C.

source.place: Lemma 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), proof, third paragraph: 'If pR_p ∉ Ass(M_p) then there exists x ∈ pR_p which is a nonzerodivisor in M_p (see Lemma 00LL) ... Hence we conclude that p is one of the associated primes of M.'

proof.text: *Filtration.* ($R$ Noetherian, $M$ finite.) By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-prime-filtration] there are $0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_n=M$ and primes $\mathfrak p_1,\dots,\mathfrak p_n$ of $R$ with $M_i/M_{i-1}\cong R/\mathfrak p_i$. Tensoring $0\to M_{i-1}\to M_i\to R/\mathfrak p_i\to0$ with the flat module $N$ gives an exact sequence of $S$-modules $0\to M_{i-1}\otimes_RN\to M_i\otimes_RN\to(R/\mathfrak p_i)\otimes_RN\to0$ (injectivity on the left and exactness in the middle by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], surjectivity on the right by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]), and $(R/\mathfrak p_i)\otimes_RN\cong N/\mathfrak p_iN$ as $S$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-exact-sequence] (second inclusion, over $S$) $\operatorname{Ass}_S(M_i\otimes_RN)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}_S(M_{i-1}\otimes_RN)\cup\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak p_iN)$, and by induction on $i$ (with $M_0\otimes_RN=0$, which has no associated prime since $\operatorname{Ann}(0)=S$ is not prime) $\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak p_iN)$.

source.place: Lemma 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), proof, last paragraph: 'Continuing the argument we choose a filtration ... with subquotients isomorphic to N/p_iN'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)$ and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$; by Claim C (Steps 4-7) $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$, and by Step 8 $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak p_iN)$ for some $i$. Now $R/\mathfrak p_i$ is a finite $R$-module (generated by $\bar1$) and $N/\mathfrak p_iN\cong(R/\mathfrak p_i)\otimes_RN$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], so Claim C applied to $R/\mathfrak p_i$ gives $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(R/\mathfrak p_i)$. And $\operatorname{Ass}_R(R/\mathfrak p_i)=\{\mathfrak p_i\}$: $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\bar0)=R$ is not prime, and for $r\notin\mathfrak p_i$, $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\bar r)=\{a:ar\in\mathfrak p_i\}=\mathfrak p_i$ as $\mathfrak p_i$ is prime. Hence $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN)$ with $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$, i.e. $\mathfrak q$ lies in the right hand side. With Steps 1 and 3 this proves equality for Noetherian $R$.
